reasoning: Sierra La Madera is the Sky Island range in the municipios of Cumpas, Granados, Huásabas, Moctezuma and Villa Hidalgo (Bermudez-Enriquez et al. 2013, USDA RMRS-P-67). GeoNames 9028461 lies between those towns: 27 km east of Cumpas and 21 km west of Huásabas on the Bavispe (pipeline/measure/distances.py). The book puts the wolf on its eastern slopes, then across the Bavispe and north, which fits a range bounded on the east by the river. Readers disagree: Bell (2000) and Joe Hazelton's map take the other Sierra de la Madera, on the upper Bavispe (GeoNames 3996948), 81 km north-east. That range lies east of the river, so from it the wolf would reach the border without crossing the Bavispe, which the text has her do.
GeoNames gives the river one point, at its mouth, about 100 km south of where the story crosses it. Rivers are drawn as lines from stage 2; crossings are stops.

GNIS 929106, the civil feature for Hidalgo County, New Mexico, formed from Grant County in 1919: the Parhams' home county, named in the opening episode (1-01) and again when Billy says where he is from (1-10). Bell 2000 (p. 68) reads it the same way.

GNIS 25442, the civil feature for Cochise County, Arizona, west of Hidalgo County across the state line: the wolf's range runs west into it from the Peloncillos (1-04). Drawn as a county point, like Grant and De Baca counties. Bell 2000 (p. 62) reads it the same way.

GNIS 896882, Taylor Draw, Hidalgo County, at its head on the western slope of the Animas Mountains, 7 km south-south-west of Animas Peak and 16 km north-east of Cloverdale (pyproj, WGS 84). The text traces the wolf up that slope to where the draw heads. Bell 2000 (p. 16) puts the draw in the same place; Joe Hazelton's map pins its mouth, which it shares with Foster Draw.

GeoNames 8716831, Cañón la Cabellera, the only canyon of the name, 3 km west of the Sierra de la Cabellera point. The text names the canyon as Billy rides south with the wolf (1-09). Bell 2000 (p. 91) indexes it.

GNIS 11603, South Fork Skeleton Canyon, Cochise County: the text names only the south fork, which the wolf crosses (1-04). GNIS has no Skeleton Creek; the main canyon (GNIS 11397) meets the fork 0.8 km east. Joe Hazelton's map pins the same fork mouth, and Bell 2000 (p. 25) agrees on the area.

GNIS 5857, Hog Canyon Spring, with Hog Canyon (GNIS 5855) 1.9 km south, in the Peloncillos just inside Arizona, where the wolf ranges (1-04) and Billy sets traps on the Hog Canyon trail (1-05, 1-06). The other Hog Canyon Springs in Arizona are far north, in Gila and Greenlee counties. Bell 2000 could not find the name on BLM maps.

GNIS 886444, the small Black Point in Hidalgo County about 4 km north of Cloverdale, not the larger Black Point in Grant County. Bell 2000 marks the same summit on his map of Hidalgo County (Figure 3.2, read to about 2 km), and Joe Hazelton's map agrees to within 30 m.

GeoNames 8688585, Serranía Pilares de Teras, at about 2,000 m inside the Bavispe's great bend south of Colonia Morelos. The text has Billy look south across the river to the range from near Colonia Oaxaca, and the river run south under its western wall after the bend, which fits this point (16 km south-west of Colonia Oaxaca, 19 km south-south-east of Morelos). GeoNames 3981872, Sierra de Teras, a rounded point that falls beside the river at about 930 m, was the earlier pick. Bell 2000 (p. 93) also has the range to Billy's south; Joe Hazelton's map pins the old mining town of Pilares de Teras, 5.6 km away.
